newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW profits surge robust 30 pct in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: BMW profits surge robust 30 pct in H1 1997.

text.p: German luxury carmaker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) said on Tuesday that group net profit surged 30 percent to 435 million marks in the first half of 1997.
The profit, which surpassed analysts' expectations, came on the back of a 15.5 percent increase in sales to 29.10 billion marks and an eight percent increase in group deliveries to 601,070 units.
The carmaker, which is known for offering conservative forecasts about future results, added that it expected sales and profit to climb for the year as a whole, but did not specify by how much.
For the first six months of 1997, analysts had expected BMW to report a jump in net profit of up to 400 million marks and sales of roughly 30 billion marks.
Investors reacted favourably to the report, pushing BMW's share price up by nine marks in early dealings to 1,479.00.
In 1996, BMW's net profit climbed 18.5 percent to 820 million marks on sales growth of 13 percent to 52.27 billion marks -- a record high.

Analysts said the solid jump in profit was due to a trio of factors -- the dollar's climb against the mark, a low base figure and good demand for BMW branded cars such as the 5-Series and Z3 roadster.
The dollar has climbed roughly 19 percent against the the mark so far this year to 1.8384, boosting sales and profits by increasing the mark value of business conducted in the huge U.S. market.
The first half of 1996, meanwhile, was unusually difficult for BMW as it updated its 5-Series model, leading consumers to hold off purchases of the previous executive class car.

Finally, analysts said BMW has captured the market's attention with high technology cars and has managed to prevent sales of its mainstay 3-Series from flagging too badly as that car nears the end of its model life.
